title: Volume 1 Chapter 3: To You Who Are Surprisingly Close, and to You Who Feel Breathtakingly Far Away 3
content: After all, the opponent is a dragon. A long battle is inevitable.
As I watched the wound on its hind leg, which I had just slashed, rapidly heal, I steeled myself, knowing that I was undoubtedly facing a dragon.
Most dragons possess incredible regenerative abilities due to their abundant magic power.
I, an ordinary adventurer, could only expect a prolonged battle rather than a quick victory. In such a scenario, the key was to avoid taking direct hits from its attacks.
No matter how confident I was in the strength of my body enhancement, repeated attacks would accumulate damage, weighing down my movements, which was the last thing I wanted when fighting a dragon.
After all, against a dragon...
"Yeah, if I can't catch it, then I'll just have to do that."
I looked up at the Forest Dragon, which had exposed its vulnerability by lifting its massive body high, gathering an immense amount of magic power in its mouth lined with fangs.
Dragon Breath, the very embodiment of destruction possessed by dragons.
I could see a dense mass of magic power that seemed ready to touch me.
Was it planning to unleash its breath directly onto the ground beneath it? As expected of a master, it was quite bold.
If it unleashed Dragon Breath right below, it would engulf not just me but also Erika and the others, who were about twenty feet away. I couldn't let that happen.
Just as my thoughts caught up with my body, I kicked off the ground and slid under the Forest Dragon's jaw instead.
I pushed my body enhancement to its limits, feeling my breath mix with magic power.
The Forest Dragon seemed to have completely lost interest in me.
No matter what happened, it was determined to blow everything away with its breath.
I captured the moment when the magic power, which seemed about to touch me, transformed.
I realized my body moved before my thoughts did, only after I swung my sword.
The Forest Dragon's lower jaw collided with its upper jaw. Looking up at the Forest Dragon's head, I thought I had succeeded.
This would either cause an accidental discharge or release the breath into empty air, I thought.
However, what happened next shocked me greatly.

After a brief moment of emptiness, the Forest Dragon's cheeks bulged, and then they burst, scattering breath everywhere. Like a fountain, multiple streams of breath rained down, causing explosions all around.
Considering the extent of the damage, it might have been better to let it unleash its breath.
Oh no, this is bad.
I realized this just as my body finally landed on the ground.
As I turned around to check on Erika and the others—were they safe?—I was met with a sight even more bizarre than the Forest Dragon scattering breath.
In the midst of the storm of destruction, Erika calmly intercepted the fragments of breath flying toward us with precise magic.

Even though the fragments of breath were far more powerful than ordinary magic, Erika effortlessly countered and nullified multiple at once. Adorned with sparkling golden magic and the white light of destruction, she smiled like a legendary hero.
Ah, as expected of Erika, I thought, but at the same time, I was also impressed by Shara.

Despite the explosions happening all around, she continued to chant the syllable magic spell without interruption. She was indeed the woman who had bravely faced a Golden Ogre even with her ribs protruding.
Her determination was on a different level; the slight rolling of her eyes seemed like an illusion.
But how distant Erika was.
In the face of the incredible scene unfolding before me, I felt the gap between Erika and myself.

Her ability to manipulate magic freely and intercept the embodiment of destruction that was Dragon Breath was nothing short of genius. It made me acutely aware of the stark contrast between her and my own mediocrity.
Carrying the handicap of being unable to use magic properly, I had struggled and fought through blood and sweat, barely managing to become a rank 4 adventurer. It was pitiful.
The timid version of myself, who could only steal glances at her from the corner of the classroom, resurfaced. Could I really stand beside someone as distant as Erika?
I regretted my own cowardice and timidity only after I had rolled three times on the ground, scattering grass.

On the fourth roll, I switched my mindset, and on the fifth, I plunged my sword into the ground, forcing my body to pin itself down. I was aware that this would put me in a disadvantageous position, but it allowed me to have a bit of leeway against the Forest Dragon's approaching foreleg.
Well, "leeway" might be an overstatement; I was merely bracing myself to be blown away again.
As I barely managed to wedge my sword between its claws and body, I was once again sent flying.
Ah, damn it. My clothes have a hole now.
I twisted my body in mid-air and landed on my feet. The smell of burning grass filled the air.

Before my vision could catch up, I felt the vibrations from the ground as the Forest Dragon charged at me. Just one moment of carelessness, just a tiny opening, and here I was. I could only imagine how angry my master would be. Damn it, another hole in my clothes.
I resolved to take a hit in exchange for a strike to buy myself some time to fully regain my stance.
With a half-hearted posture, I readied my sword and prepared to strike the Forest Dragon's snout as it charged toward me. Ah, I hated this. Complaining about my own mediocrity.
"It is a wife's duty to help her husband in times of crisis."
My enhanced hearing caught that voice, which stood out amidst the cacophony of the Forest Dragon's charge. In an instant, a fireball flew from above and collided with the Forest Dragon's head.
As it stumbled and crashed toward me, I desperately dodged. Just as I thought I was saved, the Forest Dragon's roar echoed.
Its mouth was shredded from the explosion of its own breath, its eyes burned and clouded, and a third of its head was shattered, yet the Forest Dragon remained standing.
It was truly tough.
Although its regeneration speed had slowed, it was still alive despite losing a third of its head, which was downright unfair.
Ah, but three minutes felt far away. In fact, I thought it had already passed, but was it still not over? Just as I pondered this, a voice rang out at the perfect moment.
"I'm ready!"
I felt a mix of relief and surprise at how quickly it had come.
In any case, I needed to regroup with Erika.
"Are you okay?"
As I thought this, Erika was already standing beside me. I momentarily averted my gaze from her concerned words. I was always being looked after.
Seeing my brief hesitation, Erika showed a puzzled expression. I shook my head in response, and she nodded back.
"Then let's go."
She smiled at me, as if to say that we could simply cut down anything that stood in our way, brushing her hair aside with a natural grace.
"Are you ready?"
Before I could respond, the Forest Dragon roared, glaring at us with one eye that had regained its light.
I heard Shara's panicked voice.
"I'm ready, but it's far! It's really far!"
Since I had to move around, there was about forty feet of distance between Shara and the Forest Dragon.
"I'm going to stop moving now, so get ready!"
I shouted, shaking off the gloomy mood I had been in until now. I couldn't afford to embarrass myself any further after having made Erika worry this much.
As the Forest Dragon charged at me, I swung my sword down at its snout, steeling my resolve. I held a grudge against the hole in my clothes; adventurer gear isn't cheap.
Though my strike was somewhat fueled by personal grievances, my sword technique was clean.

The Forest Dragon's upper jaw crumpled. As I locked eyes with Erika over its crushed jaw, I somehow understood what she wanted to do. I nodded lightly, and I thought I saw her smile faintly. Just making eye contact with her lifted my spirits. It was amusing how simple-minded I was, and I felt joy.

Blood and saliva from the Forest Dragon splattered everywhere, but Erika gracefully avoided them and moved to the side of the Forest Dragon. I couldn't help but widen my eyes; even with my body enhancement pushed to its limits, Erika's sword technique appeared almost ethereal.
The Forest Dragon's right foreleg lifted into the air.
It stumbled but managed to steady itself on three legs.
Instead of stabilizing, it twisted its body and aimed its tail at us.
I stepped in between Erika and the tail, raising my sword to strike the tail, which was as thick as a carriage.
Despite having dealt considerable damage, that strike felt heavier than any before.
As my arms went numb, Erika rushed toward the Forest Dragon's hind leg.
I thought she was going to sever its ankle, but her sword tip aimed for the base of its thigh.
The leg, clearly thicker than the sword Erika wielded, was cleanly severed in one stroke.

What the hell is happening? I thought, dodging the Forest Dragon as it lost its balance and began to topple toward us, and in a split second, I decided to plunge my shoulder into its massive body and push it toward Shara.
"What are you doing!?"
I answered Erika, who looked surprised by my actions.
"I'm getting it closer to Shara! Can you trust Shara to control it!?"
"I see, indeed!"
Erika replied and joined me in pushing the Forest Dragon's massive body.
"That's awful!"
I ignored Shara's words.
With all my strength, I pushed against the Forest Dragon, which was twisting and resisting with only one leg. Erika's severed foreleg and hind leg bubbled and began to regenerate.
I really hate this stubbornness of dragons.
"Now!"
Having judged that we were close enough to Shara, I leaped back, and Erika followed suit.
In that instant, Shara's voice rang out as if she had been waiting.
"Pierce through! Lux Lance!"
The unique incantation of syllable magic was declared, and the spell manifested.
Syllable magic differs from regular magic in several ways.

It requires a special vocalization for the incantation, has a trigger phrase known as a key phrase to activate the spell, and unlike regular magic, the magic circle is constructed in the external space rather than within the body, which is the most significant difference for someone like me who can see magic power.
I followed the trajectory of the light spear released from the massive magic circle constructed over Shara's head, which was several meters high.
Syllable magic boasts absurd power.
Among them, Lux Lance possesses considerable penetration and destructive power.

Even those from the church, who revere learning divine works, usually only study it as knowledge. Moreover, finding someone who can use it at a skilled speed would take more than just one hand to count throughout the entire church. It was absurd; those who could use syllable magic were practically unheard of.
After all—this was the power.

The light spear, aimed directly at the Forest Dragon, pierced its head, momentarily halting its movements before shaking its entire body and vanishing with a dry sound, taking half of the Forest Dragon with it.
There was no way this was a spell that someone aiming to heal the people with recovery magic would learn. What on earth was Shara thinking when she learned such a spell? It was outright insane.
I looked at the self-proclaimed healer, the sister.

Shara was sitting on the ground, having seemingly collapsed, breathing heavily. She must have temporarily exhausted her magic power and was overwhelmed by fatigue; her breaths were ragged. Yet her expression appeared satisfied. I wanted to point out that this was not the face of someone who had been a healer, but I held back.
"Shin."
At Erika's voice, I turned to face her.
"Is it still standing?"
I involuntarily uttered a meaningless phrase.
Thoughts of retreat crossed my mind. But Erika's voice overlapped with that thought.
"I have learned to control the fire."
In an instant, the Forest Dragon, which had been blown away yet still the size of a carriage, was engulfed in flames.
"As long as I don't burn the magic stone, it should be fine, right?"
Erika said, smiling proudly.
"I'm alive! I'm alive!"
Shara shouted, raising her fist to the sky. "Hooray! Thank you, God!" She was performing a strange dance with her trembling knees from the magic depletion.
"That was quite a good collaboration, wasn't it?"

Ignoring Shara, Erika spoke in a questioning tone. I hesitated for a moment. Which was it? Was she saying that our collaboration with Shara was good? Or was she referring to the collaboration between me and Erika? I was aware that my thoughts were heavily influenced by my own desires, but I wanted to believe it was the latter.
While I pondered, I followed the adventurer's custom and extended my right hand toward Erika. She looked at me with a puzzled expression.
Of course, it was natural; what was I expecting from a noble lady?
Even so, I shook my fist to convey how it was done, feeling slightly embarrassed.
Erika seemed to understand and clapped her right hand against her left palm, extending her left fist toward me.
"That's a good custom."
Her elegant fist bump was so characteristic of her.
"Isn't it cruel to leave me, who is trembling on my knees, out of your little world?"
Shara said, her eyes slightly teary as she extended both fists.
What a greedy person.
When I made eye contact with Erika, we gently tapped our free hands against Shara's fist.
"To meet such an end, even against a monster, is hard to bear."
That was Shara's comment, and it seemed she had recovered her magic power, standing firmly on her feet.
I couldn't tell if the expression on her face was one of exasperation or fatigue.
"I doubt it felt anything since it didn't have a head."
Erika said, continuing to burn the Forest Dragon with flames even after it had been regenerating for several minutes, showing no signs of fatigue.
I gazed at the mountain of magic stone fragments, feeling disheartened. Did I really have to search through this pile for the magic stone?

But well, Erika's objective had been achieved. To hunt the designated target for the sake of noble pride was something I, who was unqualified as a noble, honestly found hard to understand. However, if that was what Erika desired, I had no hesitation in giving it my all.

That aside, I knew that lamenting wouldn't get us anywhere, so I headed toward the mountain of magic stone fragments from the former Forest Dragon—when the moment my foot touched the ground, I felt a jolt as if I had been thrust upward.
Huh? A presence that felt like it had suddenly appeared slammed into my sense of danger.
"Shin!"
I realized I had lost precious moments as Erika called my name. As I hurriedly turned to run, I heard the ground crack behind me.
"What the hell is this!?"

Shara screamed, but her voice turned into a strange cry as Erika lifted her onto her shoulder. I caught up with Erika, running silently, my sense of crisis crushing any light-hearted banter. I heard a roar that shook the ground, and I glanced back.
"Are we really going to take down a 'castle' to earn the down payment for a house?"
A quip slipped from my lips, my light-heartedness returning almost instantly.
Looking up, I saw the massive form of the Forest Dragon, which seemed to mock us, shaking off the dirt from its body.

The word "retreat" felt more realistic than ever, my instincts as an adventurer warned me. For an adventurer, fleeing was not a disgrace. Facing an opponent that was far too overwhelming while carrying a magic-depleted Shara was simply too much.
But what about Erika's feelings? Would she accept retreat so easily? Or would she prioritize her noble pride?
"Just to clarify..."
The giant Forest Dragon roared.
"Erika, if you don't care about that house, we can escape, and there are easier opponents out there."
What should I do? I silently questioned Erika with my gaze.
The issue was whether Erika would allow us to live together outside of that house.
From my perspective, without that house, I had no justification for living with Erika. But I could come up with various reasons, like how it would be a waste of rent if we lived separately.
In the worst-case scenario, I could just grovel. I could plead for her to allow us to live together.
At my out-of-place question, Erika briefly looked anxious, while Shara, who was completely unaware of the situation, looked at me as if doubting my sanity.
After a short silence, Erika's response was simple, and I realized I had misunderstood.
Erika said.
Erika Solnzali realized she had been caught up in her own excitement.
Why hadn't she noticed it?
When Shin presented her with the option of not being bound to that house, she finally recognized that such a choice existed.
It was nothing more than her own elation over a freedom she had not wished for.
It was natural to feel giddy and flustered over something that had rolled into her life, something she had dismissed as a luxury, and to try to hold onto it, which symbolized her home in Hekatai.
For a moment, words escaped her.
She felt embarrassed for not recognizing such an obvious truth.
Without a doubt, she had assumed that Shin also wanted to live in that house, believing he was "willing" to do so.
Feeling her throat tighten as if frozen, she realized she was on the verge of tears, which surprised her.
Yet, even so, Erika felt ashamed of having felt even the slightest betrayal.
After all, Shin was merely a partner in this farce. A person with an intense, almost reckless devotion who would throw away his life just to gain a connection with someone he loved.
For her to think that she was forcing him to cohabitate with a woman he didn't love, and then to feel betrayed by his innocent acceptance of it, was something she should be ashamed of.
Reflecting on her time in Hekatai, she realized that Shin Longdagger was not someone who struggled to live alone.
She was certain that if Shin desired freedom, he would reach out for it.
Surely, he would move in whatever direction he wished, free and unfettered.
Thinking back, perhaps her interference in saving Shin earlier had been unnecessary. At that moment, she had known that Shara's incantation would soon finish and had rushed in to help.
Shin could not have been unaware of that.
Thus, when he asked, "Are you okay?" he had hesitated because he was likely confident that he could defeat the Forest Dragon on his own.

He must have wanted to ask her, "Did you choose?" To the version of herself that had been elated over the freedom that had unexpectedly come her way, he was extending a hand, urging her to choose, to grasp that freedom.
Incredibly close to Shin, she was presented with a choice. And it was a question that did not allow for retreat.
"What do you want?" For her to answer while imposing a farce upon Shin required an immense amount of courage. It was a demand to choose, to show her desire for the freedom she had received.
Erika attempted to choose, but words failed her. She had never felt this cowardly before.
So, she found herself asking again, wanting to know Shin's feelings.
"Do you prefer being alone?"
I realized, in response to Erika's question, that I had misunderstood. From the very beginning, Erika had not intended to earn the house's price for the sake of noble pride.
This... this was Erika's kindness!
A revelation struck me like lightning.
The kindness she had shown me, which allowed me to lose my justification for living with her outside of that house, was her way of fulfilling the designated subjugation.
It was a mercy given to someone who could be dismissed as merely a partner in a farce, a fool who had thrown away his life just because she claimed to love him.
I felt like shouting at my own foolishness for thinking it was about noble pride.
This was not about noble pride; it was about Erika's existence as a noble.
Do you prefer being alone? The kindness embedded in that question warmed my heart.
Thoughts surged like thunder, and my trembling throat formed the words that were only natural.
